threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's acceptable to take the Overground when you could just ride a bike to get anywhere in 15 minutes.
Last night on the 36, a guy serenaded the aisle with a ukulele, while a group in the back passed around a suspicious-looking sandwich. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids making a skate ramp out of old sofas in the park, I realized this place thrives on creativity, not just chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a U-Bahn stop where the graffiti is considered art, not vandalism—like the walls of Hallesches Tor. It's a canvas!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they stay calm when BART glitches happen—while newcomers panic, we’ve got our backup Muni routes ready.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog in a hot dog costume riding the 14. It didn't even phase the driver, just another day in the Mission, I guess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just parks and plazas, but they miss the real charm in the narrow streets where every corner hides a unique bar.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always pick them out by their confused looks at the metro maps and their insistence on calling it 'La Rambla' instead of just 'Rambla'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Underground'—everyone knows we’re too cool for that here.
Last night on the 21, a guy was yelling about how pigeons are plotting against him. Everyone just nodded like it made total sense.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted a grandma arguing with a pigeon in Hermannplatz. The pigeon won, flapping away as she shook her fist.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner Kebab stand next to a high-end gallery, showcasing a blend of street culture and art that's completely unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively avoid the BART delays by hopping on a random Muni that’ll take them halfway across the city.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in the Tenderloin offer a Muni driver a sandwich instead of fare. The driver laughed, took the sandwich, and let him ride. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals are in cafes chatting, but many are just hurrying to grab bread from the local panaderia before the morning rush.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: The way they stand in front of every menu, staring at the prices like they're in a museum, gives them away instantly.
